summary_hint: which trust/estate (name + EIN), which tax year, its total income and distributable net income, and the total distributions paid to beneficiaries

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — confirms this is a 1041 and not a personal 1040/1120

typed_core.name: form_number
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the literal "1041" form code beside the title; distinguishes trust vs estate vs grantor filings

typed_core.name: tax_year_or_period
typed_core.why: identity — which year this return covers (degraded from date_range; a fiscal-year trust may state a range, not a single year)

typed_core.name: estate_or_trust_name
typed_core.why: identity — names the filing entity (degraded from entity)

typed_core.name: ein
typed_core.why: PII + identity — the trust's taxpayer ID; the join key to K-1s and to the borrower's stated trust income
typed_core.prompt_hint: EIN format is NN-NNNNNNN; do not confuse it with a beneficiary SSN (NNN-NN-NNNN)

typed_core.name: entity_type
typed_core.why: processor — decedent's estate vs simple vs complex vs grantor trust changes how distributions are treated (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: initial_final_or_amended_return
typed_core.why: processor — a "final" return signals the trust is terminating, ending the income source (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: date_entity_created
typed_core.why: identity — establishes trust vintage; supports seasoning of the income source

typed_core.name: fiduciary_name
typed_core.why: identity/processor — the trustee who signs and can be contacted (flattened from fiduciary_name_and_address object)

typed_core.name: fiduciary_address
typed_core.why: processor — trustee contact for verification (flattened from the same object)

typed_core.name: party_names_raw
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the verbatim named-party string so a bad fiduciary/beneficiary split stays visible (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: total_income
typed_core.why: processor — top-line trust income

typed_core.name: income_distribution_deduction
typed_core.why: processor — the amount passed through to beneficiaries (drives beneficiary income)

typed_core.name: distributable_net_income
typed_core.why: processor — DNI caps the taxable portion of beneficiary distributions

typed_core.name: distributions_paid_or_required
typed_core.why: processor — the actual/required distribution total; the borrower-beneficiary's income figure

typed_core.name: taxable_income
typed_core.why: processor — trust-level taxable income after the distribution deduction

typed_core.name: total_tax
typed_core.why: processor — trust tax liability (net-income cross-check)

typed_core.name: accounting_method
typed_core.why: disambiguator — cash vs accrual changes how income/distribution figures should be read (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: fiduciary_signed
typed_core.why: processor — was the return executed by the fiduciary (degraded from signature/bool)

typed_core.name: fiduciary_signature_date
typed_core.why: processor — execution date; supports document-age testing

typed_core.name: preparer_name
typed_core.why: processor — third-party preparer independence (flattened from paid_preparer_information object)

nested_lists.name: beneficiary_k1_records
nested_lists.shape_reason: a trust genuinely has multiple beneficiaries and this is the highest-value repeating structure (it carries the borrower's distribution income and TIN); item count is small-to-moderate (typically < 20), but a flat row keeps token cost low and matches the other financial lists

fields.name: beneficiary_name
fields.why: names the beneficiary receiving the distributive share

fields.name: beneficiary_tin_masked
fields.why: the beneficiary's SSN/TIN, the join to a borrower's stated trust income
fields.pii_note: beneficiary SSN/TIN — needs its own row redactor via the nested-record (transaction-description) pattern; needs registration, pre_masked=true

fields.name: income_type
fields.why: the K-1 income-type label paired with the share amount (box 1 interest, box 5 other portfolio, etc.)

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance of the row within the return

rejected.name: issuer_name
rejected.reason: on a self-prepared 1041 the "issuer" is the trust itself; duplicates estate_or_trust_name — captured there / by preparer_name

rejected.name: issuer_address / issuer_phone / issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: contact fields with no consumer on a tax return; catch-all captures if present

rejected.name: statement_period_start / statement_period_end
rejected.reason: not a statement; the period is tax_year_or_period

rejected.name: interest_income / dividends / business_income_or_loss / capital_gain_or_loss
rejected.reason: components of total_income; no consumer distinguishes them — catch-all captures if a future rule needs a line item

rejected.name: deduction_line_items
rejected.reason: object[] with no rule; total effect is already in taxable_income; would consume the single list budget without a consumer

rejected.name: rents_royalties_partnerships_and_other_income
rejected.reason: object[] income components; no consumer; catch-all captures

rejected.name: attached_schedules_and_statements
rejected.reason: string[] inventory with no consumer; a description, not a decision input

rejected.name: accumulation_or_discretionary_terms
rejected.reason: narrative with no rule; catch-all captures

rejected.name: signature_blocks / notary_block
rejected.reason: fiduciary execution captured by fiduciary_signed; a 1041 is not notarized

encoding_variations: Tax year stated as a single year ("2025") on calendar filers but as an explicit date range on fiscal-year trusts — carry tax_year_or_period verbatim
Entity type appears both as a checkbox label ("Complex trust") and as an IRS box selection — the model must read the checked box, not merely find the word

"Distributions" appear in two places: Schedule B line (income distribution deduction) and the K-1 box 1-14 amounts; distributions_paid_or_required vs income_distribution_deduction are distinct figures; keep both so they are not conflated

open_questions.q: Second/third nested list (deduction_line_items, K-1s, other-income) — the catalog offers three object[] structures.
open_questions.recommendation: keep only beneficiary_k1_records — it is the only one with a plausible future consumer (borrower distribution income); revisit if a trust-income recipe needs line-item deductions GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

options: store raw (snapshot masks, preserves K-1 join)
pre-mask to last-4 in the extractor
open_questions.recommendation: store raw — preserves K-1 join, snapshot masks; flagging rather than deciding GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

open_questions.q: beneficiary_k1_records item shape uncertainty — beneficiary count is usually small but unbounded (a large family trust could have many).
options: reconsider shape after a real sample
open_questions.recommendation: flat-row chosen to stay under the 16,384 ceiling; confirm with a real multi-beneficiary sample

notes: No rules read this document today (rule floor is empty); every field is justified by identity, PII, disambiguation, or processor use — the "cheap future rule" test. This is a Form 1041 (U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts).
Box map for the money fields: Line 9 total income, Line 18 income distribution deduction, Line 22/23 taxable income, Line 7 Schedule B DNI, Schedule B line 10 distributions.
Each beneficiary K-1 is a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041); box 1 is interest, box 5 other portfolio income, etc. — capture the share amount and its income-type label together.
ein needs _PII_FIELDS registration (the registered employer_ein is a different field); recommend raw + snapshot masking to preserve the K-1 join.
beneficiary_tin_masked (nested) has no _PII_FIELDS path; it must carry its own redactor via the nested-record pattern and needs registration, pre_masked=true.
